say: Your database runs on five servers. One of them is the leader, and every write goes through it. Then it goes silent. Who's in charge now?
show: Your database runs on *five servers.* One of them is the [leader,] and every write goes through it. Then it goes *silent.* [Who's in charge now?]

say: The leader keeps sending a heartbeat, a tiny message that says I'm alive. When the heartbeats stop, the others know something's wrong.
show: The leader keeps sending a [heartbeat,] a tiny message that says *I'm alive.* When the heartbeats *stop,* the others know something's [wrong.]

say: Each server has its own random timer, so they rarely all jump at once. The first one to run out asks the rest: vote for me.
show: Each server has its own *random timer,* so they rarely all jump at once. The first one to run out asks the rest: [vote for me.]

say: It only wins with a majority. Out of five, that's three votes, its own included. Then it starts sending the heartbeats.
show: It only wins with a [majority.] Out of five, that's *three votes,* its own included. Then it starts sending the *heartbeats.*

say: Like a class picking a new monitor. Everyone gets one vote, and you need more than half, so there can't be two winners.
show: Like a class picking a new *monitor.* Everyone gets *one vote,* and you need more than [half,] so there can't be [two winners.]

say: That matters. If two servers both accepted writes as leader, your data would split into two versions. That's called split brain.
show: That matters. If two servers both accepted writes as leader, your data would *split* into two versions. That's called [split brain.]

say: If the network cuts the servers into three and two, only the side with three can pick a leader and save writes. The two can't.
show: If the network cuts the servers into *three and two,* only the side with [three] can pick a leader and save writes. The two *can't.*

say: And when the old leader comes back, it sees a newer election and steps down to follow.
show: And when the old leader comes back, it sees a *newer election* and [steps down] to follow.

say: You rarely build this yourself. Tools like etcd use an algorithm called Raft to run these elections for you.
show: You rarely build this yourself. Tools like *etcd* use an algorithm called [Raft] to run these elections for you.
